mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and an increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a stagflationary environment where corporate margins are squeezed, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where RSAFS declines and CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (indicating a contraction in manufacturing and mining), the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day forward returns due to reduced corporate output and investment.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeds 200,000, it indicates robust job growth that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and an increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a stimulative policy response to economic weakness, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary stimulus with consumer spending boost
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines and RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where CPIAUCSL year-over-year growth exceeds 2.5%.
